rem:descent-physical-three:
Remark Physical implications of a 3-dimensional base. At dimension 3 the physical content is richest, and two of its features exist at no lower stratum.

  1. Primordial vortex. Vortex filaments are curves in a 3-manifold, hence of codimension 2. This is the unique stratum at which they may knot and link. Every knot-theoretic statement in the framework — the braid closure, the Markov trace, the hyperbolic volume — is a statement about this stratum, and has no counterpart below it.
  2. Mass carries the knot. The surface \Sigma of the mass identity is here a 2-submanifold with boundary, and it is a genuine choice rather than being forced to be the base. Its boundary is a curve in M_k, which may be knotted. The 2-holonomy reduces under the feedback to the holonomy of that boundary, up to a central element, so at this stratum the mass retains non-abelian content and that content is the boundary knot. Descending one step closes the surface and leaves only the central part.
  3. Lepton generations. The base admits vertical harmonic forms up to degree 3 (Betti numbers on branes), the largest range in the ladder. Because the Euler characteristic is stable under descent and lifting (Euler characteristic stability), the value \chi = -6 fixed here is what every lower stratum inherits; the strata differ in the vertical degree available to realise it, not in the count itself.
cor:mass-identity-C: Corollary Archimedean realisation: nonabelian multiplicative integration. Consider the archimedean quantum observable universe (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) (\mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe) with instanton connection A, Levi form L, and self-dual curvature F^+. One realises the categorical mass (mass identity) as Yekutieli's nonabelian multiplicative integral [yekutieli2015].
prf:mass-identity-C:
Proof Proof of archimedean mass identity. Let \varrho be a closed cycle encircling a vortex filament and let \Sigma be a surface with \partial\Sigma = \varrho. The categorical mass (mass identity) is realised as Yekutieli's nonabelian multiplicative integral [yekutieli2015]:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = 
  \left\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \right\rVert,

where \mathrm{MI}\!\int_\Sigma denotes the 2-dimensional twisted nonabelian multiplicative integral, the integrand is the connection--curvature pair (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) satisfying the quantum flatness equation (eq:quantum-flatness), and \lVert\cdot\rVert is the Killing-form norm on \mathfrak{su}(2). By the nonabelian Stokes theorem [yekutieli2015], this reduces to the holonomy:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}\!\bigl(\varrho; \mathfrak{G}\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.
prop:topological-mass-upper-bound:
Proposition Upper bound for the topological decomposition of mass. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe (quantum observable universe). Let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A be a closed cycle (mass identity) whose categorical support is generated by N consecutive extensions along the brane tower (recursive brane tower) from a base-level morphism \varrho_0 \colon \mathbf{1} \to A_0. Let \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) be the trace restricted to the descended subalgebra \mathrm{im}\,\hat{\tau}_n, and let \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) be the trace restricted to the component of \ker\hat{\tau}_n localised at the i-th blow-up centre p_i (brane boundary). Then

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \bigr\rVert +
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) \bigr\rVert .
cor:quantum-dilogarithm: Corollary Quantum Dilogarithm as Localized Torsion Volume. In the archimedean realisation, the transient trace contribution \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) at the blow-up centre p_i, as defined in the topological mass upper bound, evaluates to the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(z_i). Here, z_i denotes the exact spectral coordinate of p_i within the Briggs–Klein chart (Briggs–Klein chart).
prf:quantum-dilogarithm:
Proof Proof of quantum dilogarithm corollary. The transient trace at the i-th exceptional divisor E_i \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) is the geometric integration of the q-deformed expansion flow over the resolved defect. Integrating the spectral uncertainty flow \ln_q along the radial coordinate of the Briggs--Klein affine chart yields:

\begin{equation}
\Phi_q(z_i) = \int_0^{z_i} \frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t} dt = \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^{n+1} \frac{z_i^n}{n [n]_q}
\end{equation}

where \ln_q(1+t) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^{n+1} \frac{t^n}{[n]_q} governs the continuous Reeb flow. The integration introduces the factor of n in the denominator, elevating the 1-dimensional path propagation to a geometric volume measure trapping the topological charge.
conj:topological-mass:
Conjecture Topological Decomposition of Mass. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe (quantum observable universe). Let q denote the aether parameter. Let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A be a morphism (a "closed cycle" in A, mass identity) whose categorical support is generated by N consecutive extensions along the brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} (recursive brane tower), applied to a base-level morphism \varrho_0 \colon \mathbf{1} \to A_0.

The mass \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) (mass identity) is conjectured to decompose exactly into descended and transient contributions via the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution):

\begin{equation}\label{eq:topological-mass-decomp}
  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho)
  \bigr\rVert
  + 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i)
  \bigr\rVert,
\end{equation}

where:

  1. \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) evaluates the categorical trace of (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho restricted to the descended subalgebra \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n (descent eigenspaces). Since \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \cong \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) via the ascent embedding \ell_n, this equals the mass of the base-level cycle \varrho_0. It captures the baseline drag of the Frobenius--Hopf structure along the trivial core.
  2. Each \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) evaluates the categorical trace restricted to the component of the transient complement \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n localised at the i-th blow-up centre p_i (brane boundary). The localisation remains well-defined because the kernels of \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} at distinct blow-up centres form disjoint submodules of \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}).

The idempotent splitting \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) = \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces) and the linearity of the categorical trace split the trace value additively, before norms are taken. The triangle inequality then gives the upper bound \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) \le \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \rVert + \sum_{i=1}^{N} \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) \rVert (topological mass upper bound). The conjecture is that equality holds. Equality does not follow from orthogonality of the splitting with respect to the Frobenius norm. Orthogonality gives \lVert \alpha \rVert^2 = \lVert \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2 + \lVert \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2, an additivity of squared norms, not of norms. For two non-zero orthogonal pieces the triangle inequality is in fact strict. The conjectured equality is equality in the triangle inequality, and it holds if and only if the descended trace value and all transient trace values lie pairwise on a common ray: for real values, they share a sign; for complex values, they share a phase. Whether the categorical trace values do so is the open content of the conjecture.

For the archimedean form of the bound---where the descended trace yields the holonomy \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A} and each transient trace yields the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(z_i)---see archimedean proof.

Archimedean specialisation. The categorical mass \mathrm{categoricalMass} : R \to \mathbb{R} forms the post-\tau archimedean realisation of the generic mass decomposition over a normed ground ring. It constitutes an R\to\mathbb{R} norm evaluation at q_0 and is intrinsically wall-crossing.
prop:topological-decomposition-mass:
Proposition Conjectural Topological Decomposition of Mass. The mass \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) of a vortex in any quantum observable universe (mass identity) decomposes as a sum of a descended holonomy contribution and finitely many transient contributions localised at the exceptional divisors of the brane boundary (brane boundary):

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert\mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0;\mathfrak{G})\bigr\rVert
  + 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert\Phi_q(z_i)\bigr\rVert,

where \Phi_q(z_i) gives the quantum dilogarithm (quantum dilogarithm) evaluated at the i-th blow-up centre z_i, and \varrho_0 forms the unknot core of \varrho.

Relationship to the proved theorem

The analogous decomposition for morphisms supported along the recursive brane tower (recursive brane tower) is itself conjectural (Topological Decomposition of Mass); only its upper bound is proved (upper bound). That conjecture uses the descent involution \hat\tau_n and Frobenius categorical traces to split \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) into descended and transient parts.

The present conjecture concerns the vortex case: \varrho forms a closed cycle whose support does not necessarily factor through a finite brane-tower extension. The holonomy \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A} along \varrho_0 (the flat gauge-field holonomy of the base-level connection) replaces the descent-trace part. The quantum-dilogarithm sum captures the transient blow-up contributions at the exceptional divisors of the brane boundary \partial A.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs: real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prf:topological-decomposition-mass:
Proof Proof of topological mass conjecture. Obligations.

  1. Holonomy–trace identification. Show that \bigl\lVert\mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0;\mathfrak{G})\bigr\rVert = \bigl\lVert\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho_0)\bigr\rVert when \varrho_0 is an unknot core. This requires identifying the gauge holonomy with the categorical descent trace for morphisms in the unknot class.

  2. Finite blow-up locus. Prove that the brane boundary \partial A has only finitely many exceptional divisors \{D_i\}_{i=1}^N contributing non-trivially to \mathfrak{m}(\varrho). (For a vortex, N is determined by the genus of \varrho's brane.)

  3. Quantum-dilogarithm evaluation. Show that the transient contribution at D_i equals \bigl\lVert\Phi_q(z_i)\bigr\rVert, where z_i = |\hat{V}_i(q)| is the algebraic-volume magnitude of the generator at the i-th blow-up centre.
lem:topological-mass-eigenspace-decomp:
Lemma Eigenspace decomposition of the mass integrand (descent involution). Let \alpha = (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) form the integrand of the mass identity for a vortex \varrho. Let \hat{\tau}_n be the descent involution. Suppose the multiplicative integral factors over the splitting \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}}, so that \mathrm{MI}\!\int_\Sigma \alpha = \mathrm{MI}\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \cdot \mathrm{MI}\!\int_\Sigma (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)). Then:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)
  \bigr\rVert +
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

Equality is not asserted. Killing-form orthogonality of the two parts does not supply it: orthogonality makes squared norms add, and two non-zero orthogonal vectors satisfy the triangle inequality strictly. Equality holds exactly when the two multiplicative integrals lie on a common ray, which is open.
prf:topological-mass-eigenspace-decomp:
Proof Proof of the eigenspace decomposition of the mass integrand. By the (mass identity), the mass of the vortex \varrho is

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert,

where \Sigma is a surface with \partial\Sigma = \varrho. The integrand (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) is a section of the connection--curvature bundle over \Sigma, and as such it is an element of the section algebra \Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_{n+1}, \mathrm{SU}_{q_{n+1}}(2)) at whatever level n{+}1 accommodates the vortex.

The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) decomposes this section algebra into the direct sum \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces). Since \hat{\tau}_n is an idempotent *-endomorphism, the Killing-form norm \lVert\cdot\rVert on \mathfrak{su}(2) respects the orthogonal decomposition:

  \lVert \alpha \rVert^2
  = 
  \lVert \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2 +
  \lVert \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2

for every section \alpha. Applying this to the mass integrand and using the additivity of the nonabelian multiplicative integral over orthogonal direct sums:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:mi-decomp}
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \alpha
  = 
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)
   \cdot 
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr),
\end{equation}

where the product is in the group \mathrm{SU}_{q}(2). Taking norms, the triangle inequality for the norm on \mathrm{SU}_{q}(2) gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)
  \bigr\rVert +
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

The orthogonality above gives additivity of squared norms only. It does not make this inequality an equality: for two non-zero orthogonal vectors the triangle inequality is strict. \square
lem:topological-mass-holonomy:
Lemma Descended term is the unknot-core holonomy. Consider the topological blow-up decomposition \Sigma = \Sigma_0 \cup \bigcup_{i=1}^N D_i, where \Sigma_0 forms a disc spanning the unknot core \varrho_0 and each D_i forms the exceptional disc at the i-th blow-up. Under this decomposition, the descended term equals the unknot-core holonomy:

  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)
  =
  \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}\!\bigl(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}\bigr).
prf:topological-mass-holonomy:
Proof Proof that the descended term equals the unknot-core holonomy. The projection \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n, which is isomorphic to the level-n section algebra via the ascent embedding \ell_n (descent involution). The surface \Sigma with \partial\Sigma = \varrho decomposes under the topological blow-up as \Sigma = \Sigma_0 \cup \bigcup_{i=1}^N D_i, where \Sigma_0 is a disc spanning the unknot core \varrho_0 and each D_i is the disc (exceptional divisor) inserted at the i-th blow-up. On \Sigma_0 the transient component vanishes (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) = 0 on the unknot complement, since \varrho_0 has trivial topology and all sections there factor through level n). Hence:

  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)
  = 
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{\Sigma_0} \alpha
  = 
  \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}\!\bigl(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}\bigr),

where the second equality is the nonabelian Stokes theorem [yekutieli2015] applied to the disc \Sigma_0. \square
lem:topological-mass-transient-localisat:
Lemma Transient terms are bounded by exceptional-divisor contributions. The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) operates exclusively on disjoint discs D_i centred at the blow-up points p_1, \ldots, p_N. The norm of its multiplicative integral is bounded by a sum over the exceptional divisors E_i:

  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert
  \le
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

Equality in this bound is not established. The disc splitting and the support of the integrand on E_i \subset D_i do not by themselves force it: there are data in the seminormed group \mathrm{Multiplicative}\,\mathbb{R} satisfying both for which the inequality is strict. The equality remains an open conjecture.
prf:topological-mass-transient-localisat:
Proof Proof that transient terms localise to exceptional divisors. The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) is annihilated by \hat{\tau}_n: it lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n (descent eigenspaces). By the structure of the defining boundary (brane boundary), the support of a transient section is contained in a neighbourhood of the boundary \partial \mathcal{S}_n, which has codimension \geq 2 in \mathcal{S}_n (item (1)) and whose fibre at each blow-up centre p_i is the exceptional divisor E_i \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) (item (2)).

On the surface \Sigma, the transient integrand is therefore supported on the discs D_i centred at the blow-up points. Since the D_i are disjoint (each blow-up introduces a new connected component of \partial \mathcal{S}_n), the multiplicative integral splits as an ordered product:

  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma
  \bigl(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)\bigr)
  = 
  \prod_{i=1}^{N}
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{D_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr).

Since the integrand is supported on the exceptional fibre E_i \subset D_i, each disc integral equals the corresponding exceptional-divisor integral. The norm on the structure group is a group seminorm, so it satisfies the triangle inequality \lVert gh \rVert \le \lVert g \rVert + \lVert h \rVert, and induction on N gives

  \bigl\lVert
  \prod_{i=1}^{N}
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{D_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert
  \le
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

\square

The splitting and support hypotheses do not yield equality. Commutation of the disc integrals modulo the central band \mathcal{O}_M^{\times} of the gerbe does not make the norm additive: the group \mathrm{Multiplicative}\,\mathbb{R} is commutative, and its elements \mathrm{ofAdd}(1) and \mathrm{ofAdd}(-1) have norms summing to 2 while their product \mathrm{ofAdd}(0) has norm 0. Equality would require a further structural input, for instance that the disc integrals lie on a common ray on which the norm is additive. No such input is established, and the equality remains open.
conj:topological-mass-dilogarithm:
Conjecture Symmetric q-dilogarithm evaluation of exceptional-divisor contributions. Each exceptional-divisor summand evaluates to the symmetric q-dilogarithm in the spectral coordinates of the Briggs--Klein chart at E_i:

  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i}
  \bigl(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+\bigr)
  \bigr\rVert
  =
  \int_0^{z_i} \frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}\, dt
  =
  -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z_i).

Here \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) = \sum_{n \ge 1} z^n/(n\,[n]_q) with the symmetric q-integer [n]_q. The series converges for |z| < q; for other z_i > -1 both sides are meant by analytic continuation. The algebraic chart relation itself imposes no restriction on the domain of z_i. This is not the product \Phi_q(z) = \prod_{k\ge1}(1-q^{-k}z)^{-1}; see the disambiguation.
rem:topological-mass-dilogarithm-sketch: Remark Argument sketch for the symmetric q-dilogarithm evaluation. Sketch. Integrating the q-deformed expansion flow over the resolved defect E_i in the spectral coordinates of the Briggs--Klein chart should give \int_0^{z_i} \ln_q(1+t)/t\, dt. The missing step is the evaluation of the non-abelian multiplicative integral in that chart. The second equality, \int_0^{z} \ln_q(1+t)/t\, dt = -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z), is termwise integration of the series for \ln_q (see the proof of the mass-endomorphism tower).
prf:topological-mass:
Proof Proof of Topological Decomposition of Mass. The proof proceeds in four steps: decomposition of the mass integral using the descent involution, identification of the descended term with the unknot-core holonomy, localisation of the transient terms to exceptional divisors, and evaluation via the symmetric q-dilogarithm.

By (eigenspace decomposition of the mass integrand), the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n produces an orthogonal Killing-form decomposition of the multiplicative integral. Orthogonality makes squared norms add, not norms; for the norms themselves the triangle inequality gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \bigr\rVert +
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_\Sigma (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert.

By (descended term is the unknot-core holonomy), the first summand equals \lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \rVert. By (transient terms are bounded by exceptional-divisor contributions), the second summand is at most \sum_{i=1}^{N} \lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i} (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) \rVert. Combining these yields

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \bigr\rVert +
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{MI}\!\!\int_{E_i} (\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+) \bigr\rVert,

the upper bound of prop:topological-mass-upper-bound in its archimedean form, and an upper bound for the conjectured decomposition eq:topological-mass-decomp. Equality, and hence the conjectured decomposition itself, would need equality in both inequalities above. Both are open: neither is forced by the disc splitting and support hypotheses. If each exceptional-divisor summand equals the symmetric q-dilogarithm -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z_i), as the symmetric q-dilogarithm evaluation conjectures, then the bound reads \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) \le \lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \rVert + \sum_{i=1}^{N} \bigl(-\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z_i)\bigr). \square
ex:topological-mass-su2:
Example Topological mass decomposition for \mathrm{SU}(2). Continuing the descent eigenspaces for SU(2), one verifies the topological mass conjecture for G = \mathrm{SU}(2).

The decomposition. By the topological mass theorem, the mass of a cycle \varrho decomposes according to the eigenspace splitting:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) =  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) + \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho),

where \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}} = \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \rVert gives the descended (persistent) contribution and \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}} = \lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho) \rVert gives the transient contribution.

Descended mass. The descended trace \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}} factors through the projection \hat{\tau} onto \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \cong \mathfrak{su}(2). For the Hopf fibration \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1, the descended mass of the fundamental cycle evaluates to:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{desc}} =  \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) =  2,

which is the Euler characteristic of \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2. This provides the topologically protected part. It remains invariant under continuous deformations of the cycle and the metric.

Transient mass. The transient trace \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}} captures fluctuations in the cotangent directions \mathfrak{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} \cong \Omega^1(\mathbb{CP}^1) \oplus \mathbb{C}. For a cycle \varrho that is \mathrm{U}(1)-equivariant, \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho) = 0 since the transient eigenspace has non-zero \mathrm{U}(1)-weight. Non-equivariant deformations of \varrho contribute a non-zero \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}} that measures the departure from the symmetric configuration.

Total mass. For the fundamental cycle of the Hopf fibration, m = 2 + 0 = 2, recovering the Euler characteristic. For a deformed cycle, m = 2 + \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{trans}}, with the correction depending on the L^2-norm of the cotangent component.
sec:gb-spectral-sequence-intro:
Six mass terms as spectral-sequence pages.

The descending Gröbner–Shirshov ideal filtration J^\bullet(q) on the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) induces a spectral sequence. For semisimple H_n(R, q) its limit page is concentrated in total degree 0, and its E_\infty page governs homological shell condensation and the motivic Galois coaction per cell.
prop:gb-spectral-sequence:
Proposition Length-filtration spectral sequence of the Hochschild complex of H_n(R, q). Setting. Let R be a commutative ring and q \in R^\times. The Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is free over R with standard basis \{T_w : w \in S_n\} [geckpfeiffer2000], and for a simple reflection s

\[
  T_s T_w \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    T_{sw}, & \ell(sw) = \ell(w) + 1, \\
    (q - q^{-1})\,T_w + T_{sw}, & \ell(sw) = \ell(w) - 1,
  \end{cases}
\]

where \ell is the Coxeter length (the number of inversions). Write N = \ell(w_0) = n(n-1)/2.

Definition (length filtration). For a \in \mathbb{Z} put L_a = \operatorname{span}_R\{T_w : \ell(w) \le a\}. On the Hochschild cochains C^k = \operatorname{Hom}_R\bigl(H_n(R, q)^{\otimes k}, H_n(R, q)\bigr) put

  F^p C^k \;=\; \bigl\{\, f \in C^k \;:\; f(L_{a_1} \otimes \cdots \otimes L_{a_k}) \subseteq L_{a_1 + \cdots + a_k - p} \text{ for all } a_1, \dots, a_k \,\bigr\}.

Equivalently, F^p C^k is spanned by the elementary cochains T_{w_1} \otimes \cdots \otimes T_{w_k} \mapsto T_v of weight \ell(w_1) + \cdots + \ell(w_k) - \ell(v) \ge p.

Proposition (length spectral sequence). Let d be the Hochschild differential of H_n(R, q) with coefficients in itself, and index pages E_r^{p,k} by the filtration degree p and the cochain degree k.

  1. L_a L_b \subseteq L_{a+b}, and d(F^p C^k) \subseteq F^p C^{k+1}, so (C^\bullet, d, F^\bullet) is a filtered cochain complex with a spectral sequence (E_r^{p,k}, d_r), d_r \colon E_r^{p,k} \to E_r^{p+r,k+1}.
  2. E_1^{p,k} is the weight-p part of HH^k\bigl(\operatorname{gr}_L H_n, \operatorname{gr}_L H_n\bigr), where \operatorname{gr}_L H_n is the nil-Coxeter algebra: basis \{\bar T_w\} with \bar T_u \bar T_w = \bar T_{uw} if \ell(uw) = \ell(u) + \ell(w) and 0 otherwise.
  3. In cochain degree k the filtration is finite, with weights in [-N, kN]. Hence E_r^{\bullet,k} = E_\infty^{\bullet,k} for r > (k+2)N, and
  E_\infty^{p,k} \;\cong\; \operatorname{gr}^p HH^k\bigl(H_n(R, q), H_n(R, q)\bigr).

When R is a field over which H_n(R, q) is split semisimple, the abutment is the centre Z(H_n(R, q)) in degree 0, of rank the number of partitions of n, and 0 in positive degree.

Proof.

(1) Multiplicativity. If \ell(w) \le b, the displayed rule shows that T_s T_w lies in L_{b+1}. Writing T_u = T_{s_1} \cdots T_{s_a} along a reduced word of u and inducting on a gives T_u L_b \subseteq L_{a+b}, hence L_a L_b \subseteq L_{a+b}.

Filtration preservation. The Hochschild differential is

\[
  (d f)(x_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_k)
  \;=\;
  x_0\, f(x_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_k)
  + \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} (-1)^{i+1} f(x_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_i x_{i+1} \otimes \cdots \otimes x_k)
  + (-1)^{k+1} f(x_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes x_{k-1})\, x_k .
\]

Let f \in F^p C^k and x_i \in L_{a_i}, and put A = a_0 + \cdots + a_k. The first term lies in L_{a_0} L_{A - a_0 - p} \subseteq L_{A - p}. In the middle terms x_i x_{i+1} \in L_{a_i + a_{i+1}}, so each lies in L_{A - p}. The last term is symmetric to the first. Hence d f \in F^p C^{k+1}. The identity d \circ d = 0 holds for every associative R-algebra, and a filtered cochain complex has a spectral sequence with E_0^{p,\bullet} = F^p C^\bullet / F^{p+1} C^\bullet [weibel1994].

(2) The first page. The filtrations are split by the standard basis, so \operatorname{gr}^p C^k is the span of the elementary cochains of weight exactly p, and d_0 is the weight-preserving part of d. In the product T_u T_w only the coefficient of T_{uw} with \ell(uw) = \ell(u) + \ell(w) has top weight: by induction on \ell(u) using the displayed rule, T_u T_w = T_{uw} when the lengths add and T_u T_w \in L_{\ell(u)+\ell(w)-1} otherwise. So the weight-preserving part of the multiplication is the nil-Coxeter product, and d_0 is the Hochschild differential of \operatorname{gr}_L H_n restricted to weight p. Taking cohomology gives E_1.

(3) Convergence. An elementary cochain in C^k has weight between 0 - N = -N and kN - 0 = kN, so F^{-N} C^k = C^k and F^{kN+1} C^k = 0. A differential d_r out of E_r^{p,k} lands in filtration degree p + r \le (k+1)N with p \ge -N, so it vanishes for r > (k+2)N, and one into E_r^{p,k} vanishes for r > (k+1)N. A finite filtration of each cochain group gives the stated convergence [weibel1994]. For a split semisimple algebra, HH^0 is the centre and HH^k = 0 for k > 0, since such an algebra is separable. \qquad\blacksquare

Example (n = 3). An exact computation over \mathbb{F}_P at q = 2 and q = 3, for two primes P, gives the following. In cochain degree 0, E_1 = E_\infty has one class in each of the filtration degrees 0, -2, -3, matching the rank-3 centre of H_3. In degree 1, E_1 has classes in filtration degrees 0 and -2. In degree 2, E_1 is two-dimensional in filtration degree 2. The differentials d_1 and d_3 vanish, while d_2 and d_4 each have rank 1 from degree 1 to degree 2. So E_5 = E_\infty and the sequence does not collapse at E_2.

rem:gb-spectral-sequence-interpretation:
Remark Open questions, structural value, and the Picard–Lefschetz archimedean realisation. Open formalization requirements.

Standard Hochschild-complex theory yields d \circ d = 0 and E_\infty convergence. The open requirements are:

  1. Term-by-term identification of E_\infty^{p, *} with the six mass-formula components. For p \geq 1, identifying \Phi_q poles and chirality demands explicit page computation.
  2. Explicit E_1 page computation for H_3(R, q). Burciu and Scheimbauer (2019) establish that \dim H^k(H_n(R, q), H_n(R, q)) grows via a specific partition generating function. The pairing with \mathrm{tr}_M isolates the cyclic part. Matching this to the six terms requires a computational derivation.

The Hochschild complex guarantees the existence of the spectral sequence. Matching its pages to the mass-formula terms remains open.

Rigorous derivation path

A rigorous derivation requires four steps:

  • Construct the Hochschild cochain complex C^*(H_n(R, q), H_n(R, q)) with the filtration induced by J^\bullet(q).
  • Prove \mathrm{tr}_M forms a Hochschild cocycle, exploiting the cyclicity of the Markov trace.
  • Compute the spectral sequence pages E_r explicitly for n = 3 and verify the decomposition.
  • Match each page to the corresponding mass term via \Phi_q poles, Frobenius invariants, and chirality components.

This represents a research-level project in cohomological algebra and deformation theory. One flags the target; the work remains open.

Structural value

The spectral-sequence framing enforces architectural rigidity:

  1. The six mass terms are structurally constrained. They constitute the non-trivial pages of a canonical spectral sequence.
  2. The mass sum equals the total cohomology of the filtered Hecke algebra paired with T_w.

Relation to standard formalisms

Hochschild cohomology HH^*(H_n(R, q)) is established by Kosmann-Schwarzbach, Lambe–Stasheff, and Burciu–Scheimbauer. These supply deformation-theoretic data: HH^2 controls deformations, HH^3 controls obstructions.

The filtration J^\bullet(q) incorporates the specific aether parameter q, forming a finer grading than standard length. This yields q-dependent differentials.

Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants at roots of unity emerge as residues of the E_\infty pages when q = \zeta_\ell collapses the filtration. The RT evaluation operates strictly as a spectral-sequence specialization.

This grounds the mass formula in quantum topology and deformation theory. The unification objective seeks to prove the six-term mass evaluates a specific spectral-sequence cohomology class paired against the atomic braid, relying exclusively on the Hecke algebra.

Archimedean realization

The E_\infty-pairing operates strictly over the categorical base ring R. Pairings \langle \mathrm{tr}_M, E_\infty^{p,*}(T_w)\rangle evaluate in R, not \mathbb{C}.

Applying the archimedean fibre functor \tau \colon R \hookrightarrow \mathbb{C} promotes the E_\infty-pairing to a contour integral on the Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q(\mathbb{C}). The level-p stratum maps to the geometric jet bundle J^p\mathcal{S}. The Seiberg–Witten differential \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(p)} serves as the tautological section.

The pairing's \mathbb{C}-realization gives the Picard–Lefschetz thimble period \Pi^{(p)}, equaling \tau\bigl\langle\mathrm{tr}_M, E_\infty^{p,*}(T_w)\bigr\rangle up to the integer intersection numbers n_\sigma^{(p)} of the Lefschetz decomposition. The spectral sequence and the PL thimble decomposition provide two presentations of identical data across the archimedean wall.
prop:spectral-sequence-collapse:
Proposition Limit page of the GB spectral sequence for semisimple H_n(R, q). Let R be a field and q \in R such that A = H_n(R, q) is semisimple and separable over R. Then Hochschild cohomology vanishes in positive degrees, \mathrm{HH}^k(A,\, A) = 0 for k \geq 1. Hence the limit page of the GB filtration spectral sequence is concentrated in total degree 0, with E_\infty^{0,0} = \mathrm{HH}^0(A, A) = Z(A).

This does not say the sequence collapses at E_1: a zero abutment in positive degree is compatible with non-zero E_1 terms that are cancelled by differentials.
conj:homological-shell-condensation:
Conjecture Homological shell condensation: BB-stratified E_\infty^{p,>0}(n) = 0 at magic n.

Setup

Fix a level n \in \mathbb{N} in the brane tower, with associated descent-graded jet algebra A_n = A_{n-1} \otimes \Omega^1(A_{n-1}) (def:direct-limit-algebra). The Białynicki-Birula stratification of \mathrm{Spec}(A_n) under the \mathbb{C}^\times-action induced by the descent involution \hat\tau [bialynicki1973] produces a filtration

  F^0 A_n \supset F^1 A_n \supset \cdots \supset F^p A_n \supset \cdots

with associated graded \mathrm{gr}_F A_n. The Gröbner–Shirshov spectral sequence (prop:gb-spectral-sequence) on this filtration converges to the descent-graded algebra:

  E_1^{p,q} \;=\; H^q\bigl(\mathrm{gr}_F^p A_n\bigr)
  \;\Longrightarrow\;
  H^{p+q}\bigl(A_n\bigr).

The strict-positive part E_\infty^{p, >0}(n) measures the non-trivial cohomology supported above the E_2-collapse line. Operationally, it measures the obstruction to reading the descent-graded trace purely from the diagonal.

Statement

Conjecture (homological shell condensation). For every n \in \mathfrak{M} = \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}, the Białynicki-Birula spectral sequence on A_n collapses entirely above the E_2 line:

  E_\infty^{p, q}(n) \;=\; 0
  \qquad\text{for all } p \in \mathbb{N}, \; q > 0,
  \quad n \in \mathfrak{M}.

Equivalently, the descent-graded trace \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} on J^\ell / J^{\ell+1} is supported entirely on the diagonal at saturated n, and the brane-tower descent residues vanish for \ell \geq 2.
rem:homological-shell-condensation-motiv: Remark Motivation: the Białynicki-Birula spectral sequence and shell closure. The Białynicki-Birula stratification of the brane tower (recursive-brane-tower, brane-tower-levels) under the descent involution \hat\tau (descent-involution) yields a spectral sequence whose E_\infty page records the failure of categorical neutrality at each level. The proposition names the homological condensation at saturated n. The higher pages collapse to zero, encoding shell closure as an algebraic-geometry condition on the brane-tower stratification.
rem:homological-shell-condensation-inter:
Remark Condensation terminology, conditional categorical-neutrality, and supporting evidence.

Terminology: "condensation"

The vanishing E_\infty^{p, >0}(n) = 0 dictates that every higher descent residue collapses onto the diagonal. There are no off-diagonal jet-tower contributions at saturated n. The shell condenses into a single graded piece. For n \notin \mathfrak{M} the off-diagonal pieces survive. They provide the algebraic content of non-saturation (residual capacity to absorb crossing energy).

The phenomenology this picks up is standard. At n \in \mathfrak{M} the binding-energy curve flattens, the next nucleon adds nearly-zero binding, and the shell is mathematically "full". The refactor identifies this directly in the spectral sequence, rather than via shell-model fitting.

Conditional content via the categorical-neutrality conjecture

Conditional on Categorical neutrality of saturated shells: full-twist identity action on \Phi_n at magic n, the full-twist \Delta_n^2 acts as the identity on \Phi_n at n \in \mathfrak{M}. The categorical neutrality forces the Wedderburn support of \Phi_n onto self-conjugate partitions. Pairing this with Yekutieli rigidity [yekutieli2010], the descent involution \hat\tau inherits the corresponding self-conjugacy on A_n, and the BB stratification becomes self-dual: the strata above the E_2 collapse line cancel pairwise. The conjectured E_\infty^{p, >0}(n) = 0 forms the algebraic-geometry crystallisation of this cancellation.

This conditional structure justifies authoring both conjectures together. The categorical conjecture forms the Hecke-side content; the homological conjecture forms its brane-tower-side image under Yekutieli rigidity. A proof of either implies the other under the aether axioms.

Relation to the Hoefsmit / matrix-evaluation programme

Numerical verification at k = 3, \dots, 10 (conj:magic-numbers-from-q) empirically confirms E_\infty^{p, >0}(n) = 0 at n = 2, 8, 20 via direct computation of descent residues from Hoefsmit matrices. The combinatorial blow-up at k \geq 12 blocks the matrix-evaluation approach. The homological framework analytically bypasses this barrier by replacing per-partition matrix computation with spectral-sequence arithmetic (rem:k12-barrier-bypass).

Operator-level support (clarification)

The "Wedderburn support of \Phi_n onto self-conjugate partitions" in §"Conditional content" above describes operator-level support. \Phi_n has zero matrix entries on non-self-conjugate isotypical components, but the operator on the self-conjugate components is generically non-trivial. It is not the Plancherel-weighted character sum \sum_{\lambda = \lambda'} w_\lambda \chi^\lambda, which vanishes identically at certain atomic-braid cycle types. The E_\infty^{p, >0}(n) = 0 collapse condition stated above is precisely operator-level (page collapse on the associated graded algebra). It remains consistent with this reading.

Discussion

This remains conjectural. The supporting evidence comprises:

  1. Numerical verification at n \in \{2, 8, 20\} via the matrix-evaluation programme.
  2. Conditional equivalence with Categorical neutrality of saturated shells: full-twist identity action on \Phi_n at magic n under Yekutieli rigidity (the Hecke-side conjecture is stated independently).
  3. Phenomenological agreement: the seven values \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} form the only nucleon counts at which the experimental binding curve exhibits a discontinuous first-derivative drop (the empirical signature of shell closure).

The downstream cone affects the higher-magic-number predictions n \in \{50, 82, 126\} where matrix evaluation remains unavailable. Any result quoting these higher-magic-number predictions therefore depends on this conjecture, and stays conjectural until either the conjecture is proved or the prediction is demoted to a numerical empirical claim.
cor:hecke-length-limit-page-vanishing:
Corollary Vanishing above the diagonal of the length-filtered limit page, at every n. Let R be a field of characteristic 0 and q \in R with [k]_q \neq 0 for 1 \le k \le n. Let E_r^{p,q'} be the spectral sequence of the Hochschild complex of H_n(R, q) filtered by Coxeter length, in the bigrading q' = k - p with k the cochain degree (length-filtration spectral sequence). Then

  E_\infty^{p, q'} = 0 \qquad \text{for all } p \ge 0,\ q' > 0 .

This holds for every n. In particular it holds for every real q > 1 and every n.

Proof. The hypothesis on [k]_q makes H_n(R, q) semisimple [dipper-james1986]. A semisimple algebra over a field of characteristic 0 is separable, so HH^k(H_n, H_n) = 0 for k \ge 1 [weibel1994] (limit page for semisimple H_n). The spectral sequence converges with E_\infty^{p,q'} \cong \mathrm{gr}^p HH^{p+q'}. For p \ge 0 and q' > 0 the total degree p + q' is at least 1, so E_\infty^{p,q'} = 0. For real q > 1, [k]_q = (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1}) > 0. \qquad\blacksquare

At n = 3 the exact computation gives E_\infty in cochain degree 0 only, at filtration degrees 0, -2, -3; those classes have q' = -p \ge 0 and p \le 0, consistent with the corollary.
conj:qou-motivic-galois-instance:
Conjecture QOU \mathrm{MotivicGaloisCharacter} instance via Habiro \to \mathrm{Frob}_p.

QOU MotivicGaloisCharacter instance via Habiro evaluation

The QOU brane-tower aether carries a concrete instance of Motivic Galois character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A of the Frobenius--Hopf aether constructed by the Habiro evaluation map:

  \mathrm{Frob}_p \;=\; f(u) \big|_{u = \zeta_{2p}}
  \;\in\; \mathbb{Z}[\zeta_{2p}].

Here f(u) = \sum_{m \geq 0} a_m(u) (u; u)_m represents the Habiro cyclotomic expansion of the atomic Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w, q) and u = q^{1/2}. The cyclotomic Pochhammer (u; u)_m vanishes for m \geq 2p. This forces the sum to terminate after a finite number of terms.

The finite-place compatibility checks, the downstream consumers, and cross-prime coherence are recorded in the follow-on remark; the per-cell \mathrm{Frob}_p data appears in the accompanying example.

Why this is stated as a conjecture. The formula above specifies \mathrm{Frob}_p in \mathbb{Z}[\zeta_{2p}], one prime at a time. What Motivic Galois character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A of the Frobenius--Hopf aether asks for is a single \mathrm{frobenius\_at} \colon \mathrm{Primes} \to \widehat{M}, so the content of the claim is that these per-prime evaluations cohere into one \widehat{M}-valued function. The follow-on remark argues that coherence structurally from the Habiro theorem; it is not proved. Calling this a definition would assert the construction was already in hand.

Status. No construction of this instance is available. The derivation of the perpetual obstruction from the prime-ideal collapse (C = a_0(-1) + 2 a_1(-1)) proves statements about the perpetual obstruction and constructs no motivic Galois character; it is a different result.
rem:qou-motivic-galois-instance-verifica:
Remark Construction, verification, and coherence of the QOU \mathrm{Frob}_p instance.

Construction, verification, and coherence of the QOU \mathrm{Frob}_p instance

This remark records the finite-place coherence checks, the status of the instance, the downstream consumers, and the cross-prime coherence of the QOU \mathrm{MotivicGaloisCharacter} instance via Habiro \to \mathrm{Frob}_p construction.

Construction and verification

  • Compatibility verification. One performs two finite-place coherence checks on every (p, \text{atom}) cell. First, Galois-norm integrality holds: the trace N(\mathrm{Frob}_p) = \sum_{\sigma \in \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{2p})/\mathbb{Q})} \sigma(\mathrm{Frob}_p) yields a rational integer (residual < 10^{-7}). Second, Weil purity holds at small primes: at p \in \{2, 3\}, the orbit-spread \max|\sigma(\mathrm{Frob}_p)| - \min|\sigma(\mathrm{Frob}_p)| remains below 10^{-10} for every atom, and the inferred weight w = 2 \log_p |\mathrm{Frob}_p| takes integer or near-integer values. At larger primes, the spread grows. The QOU motive remains mixed in general, consistent with the brane tower forming a sum across cohomology degrees.

  • Status: there is no instance. The motivic Galois character consists of a single datum, the Frobenius assignment \mathrm{frobenius\_at}, and nothing supplies it for the QOU aether, so Motivic Galois character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A of the Frobenius--Hopf aether is not discharged here.

Downstream consumers

Were the instance in hand, theorems that carry Motivic Galois character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A of the Frobenius--Hopf aether as a hypothesis could consume it directly, and the motivic perpetual obstruction would become unconditional for the QOU aether. That is the intended payoff, not a present fact: the instance is conjectural, so those theorems still carry the hypothesis.

What is unconditional is a narrower result on a different route: the obstruction is derived directly from the prime-ideal-collapse invariant C = a_0(-1) + 2 a_1(-1), without going through a motivic Galois character at all.

Coherence

Cross-prime coherence follows structurally from the Habiro theorem. Any two evaluations f|_{u = \zeta_{2p}} and f|_{u = \zeta_{2q}} extract from the same Habiro element and respect the natural Galois action on \mathbb{Q}(\mu_\infty). The deeper \ell-adic archimedean Weil/Deligne behaviour lies outside this construction.

sec:categorical-mass-foundations-intro: This section turns to the algebraic backbone of the real trace functional over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]. Under the descent involution \hat{\tau}, the categorical mass endomorphism splits into a descended observable eigenspace and a transient correction. This section establishes the categorical eigenspace decomposition, connects the Hecke trace to the Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov connection and Gibbs free energy, and formulates the Gröbner–Shirshov normal-form expansion and Littlewood–Richardson branching rules across multi-nucleon tensor products.
lem:topological-mass-cat-eigenspace:
Lemma Eigenspace decomposition of the categorical mass integrand. Let \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho form the categorical mass integrand of a closed cycle \varrho. When the Frobenius pairing is compatible with the *-involution, the descent involution \hat{\tau}_n produces an orthogonal decomposition of \alpha into descended and transient components, giving

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)^2
  =
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert^2
  +
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert^2.

(Orthogonal components add in quadrature, not linearly. The descended and transient traces are orthogonal, so the masses combine by the Pythagorean law, not additively.)
prf:topological-mass-cat-eigenspace:
Proof Proof of the eigenspace decomposition (categorical). By the (mass identity), the mass of \varrho is

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}\bigl(
    (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id})
    \circ \Delta
    \circ \varrho
  \bigr)
  \bigr\rVert.

The integrand \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho is an element of \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}). The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) decomposes this algebra into the direct sum \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces):

  \alpha =  \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) +  (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)).

When the Frobenius pairing is compatible with the *-involution (\langle \alpha^*, \beta \rangle = \overline{\langle \alpha, \beta \rangle}), the idempotent decomposition is orthogonal with respect to the Frobenius norm. Therefore:

  \lVert \alpha \rVert^2
  = 
  \lVert \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2
  + 
  \lVert \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2,

The categorical trace is linear, so \mathrm{tr}(\alpha) = \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) + \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)), and the same *-compatibility carries the descended/transient orthogonality through the trace: \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \perp \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)). Orthogonal vectors add in quadrature, not linearly (additivity would require alignment, not orthogonality), so the Pythagorean identity gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)^2
  = 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  \bigr\rVert^2
  + 
  \bigl\lVert
  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  \bigr\rVert^2.

\square
lem:topological-mass-cat-descended:
Lemma Descended term equals the base-level mass. Let \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho form the categorical mass integrand of a closed cycle \varrho at level n+1. Let \varrho_0 denote its base-level descent. Then

  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \bigr\rVert
  =
  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho_0).
prf:topological-mass-cat-descended:
Proof Proof that the descended term equals the base-level mass. The projection \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n, which is isomorphic to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) via the ascent embedding \ell_n (descent involution). The compatibility of the categorical trace with descent (\mathrm{tr}_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} = \mathrm{tr}_{n+1} on \mathrm{im}\hat{\tau}_n) gives:

  \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}(\ell_n(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\alpha)))
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_n(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\alpha))
  = 
  \mathrm{tr}_n(\alpha_0),

where \alpha_0 = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho_0 is the mass integrand of the base-level cycle. Hence \lVert \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \rVert = \mathfrak{m}(\varrho_0). \square
lem:topological-mass-cat-transient:
Lemma Transient terms localise to blow-up centres (categorical). The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} has support contained in the union of the kernels of \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} at the blow-up centres p_1, \ldots, p_N. The transient trace decomposes as a sum of disjoint local contributions:

  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  = 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i).
prf:topological-mass-cat-transient:
Proof Proof that transient terms localise (categorical). The transient component \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) lies in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\hat{\tau}_n. By the structure of the brane boundary, the support of a transient endomorphism is contained in the union of the kernels \ker(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}|_{p_i}) at the blow-up centres p_1, \ldots, p_N. These kernels are mutually disjoint submodules because each arises from a distinct extension step. The transient trace therefore decomposes as a sum:

  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  = 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i).

The disjointness of the supports ensures that the norm of the sum equals the sum of the norms. \square
prf:topological-mass-categorical:
Proof Categorical proof of the topological decomposition of mass. One assembles the bound from three lemmas. Put \alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho. By (eigenspace decomposition), the descent involution splits \alpha as \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) + (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)). Since the trace is linear, the trace value splits the same way:

  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha)
  =
  \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) +
  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)).

By (descended term equals base mass), the first summand is \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho), the trace of the base-level cycle \varrho_0. By (transient terms localise to blow-ups), the second summand is \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i). Taking norms, the triangle inequality gives

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = \lVert \mathrm{tr}(\alpha) \rVert
  \le
  \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho) \bigr\rVert +
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \bigl\lVert \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i) \bigr\rVert .

Orthogonality of the splitting with respect to the Frobenius norm would add squared norms, not norms, so it does not upgrade this bound to the equality of the topological decomposition of mass. \square
